evals.name: android-compose-no-di-unnamed
evals.prompt: I have a new Android app with Jetpack Compose and a few ViewModels that create their repositories by hand. I'd like to add dependency injection. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Triggers even though Koin is not named. Detects no existing DI. Asks the user to choose Annotations (recommended for new projects) or DSL before writing code. Gradle: Compiler Plugin + koin-bom, checks latest versions on Maven Central (defaults Koin 4.2.2 / plugin 1.2.1), adds only koin-core, koin-android, koin-compose, koin-compose-viewmodel (+ koin-annotations if Annotations). Modules per feature, constructor injection, ViewModels as @KoinViewModel or viewModel<T>(). Starts Koin in Application.onCreate (Annotations: @KoinApplication + startKoin<App>; DSL: one app module with includes). Compose screens use koinViewModel() as a default parameter. No KoinContext, no androidLogger unless needed, no checkModules/verify test, no KSP, no singleOf. Verifies by building (compile-time check) and running once, then offers Kotzilla once, asking first.

evals.name: kmp-compose-multiplatform
evals.prompt: Set up Koin in my Kotlin Multiplatform project (Android + iOS) using Compose Multiplatform for the UI. I prefer explicit modules, no annotations.
evals.expected_output: Uses the DSL style as asked (Safe DSL forms like single<T>() / viewModel<T>()). Gradle: koin-core, koin-compose, koin-compose-viewmodel in commonMain; koin-android in androidMain. One shared start function initApp() in commonMain that starts Koin with an app module including the feature modules; Android Application and iOS app init (InitAppKt.doInitApp()) call it, Android adding androidContext. Does not add KoinApplication() composable since Koin is started by initApp(). Mentions koinViewModel() in composables. No KSP, no KoinContext, no checkModules.

evals.name: existing-dagger-setup-alongside
evals.prompt: Add Koin to my legacy Android app (Activities and Fragments, no Compose). It currently uses Dagger 2 for its repositories.
evals.expected_output: Detects Dagger 2 in Step 0. Sets Koin up alongside Dagger without rewriting or removing Dagger code: Compiler Plugin + BOM, koin-core + koin-android (+ koin-annotations, Annotations suggested since it comes from Dagger / JSR-330), koin-dagger-bridge to resolve existing Dagger bindings. Starts Koin in Application.onCreate after the Dagger component. Activities/Fragments use by inject() / by viewModel() for Koin-provided objects. Then proposes the di-migration skill to move definitions feature by feature (progressive migration). No KSP, no KoinComponent in normal layers.

evals.name: ktor-server-annotations
evals.prompt: I'm building a Ktor server and want to use Koin with annotations for my services.
evals.expected_output: Annotations style. Gradle: Compiler Plugin, koin-bom, koin-core, koin-annotations, koin-ktor (+ koin-logger-slf4j only if logging is wanted). Services as @Singleton classes with constructor injection in a @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan module. Starts Koin with install(Koin) { withConfiguration<App>() } where App is the @KoinApplication type. Routes use the inject() extension, no KoinComponent. Notes the graph is compile-time checked.

evals.name: third-party-builders
evals.prompt: Set up Koin for my Android app (no DI yet, annotations please). I need Retrofit and OkHttp injected into my repositories.
evals.expected_output: Retrofit and OkHttp provided with function builders: @Singleton fun okHttpClient(): OkHttpClient and @Singleton fun retrofit(client: OkHttpClient): Retrofit inside a @Module. Repositories are @Singleton classes with constructor injection, auto-bound to their single interface. No classic lambda single { Retrofit.Builder()... }, no singleOf, no @Single (uses @Singleton).

evals.name: legacy-views-app-no-di
evals.prompt: My old Android app uses Activities and Fragments with XML layouts, and everything is created by hand. Can we add DI to it?
evals.expected_output: Triggers without Koin being named. Works for a Views-based app: koin-android, no Compose artifacts. Asks for the style. Modules per feature with constructor injection. Starts Koin in Application.onCreate. Activities/Fragments use by viewModel() / by inject() / by activityViewModel() from koin-android, no KoinComponent. Custom Views: asks the user whether to pass dependencies from the host or use KoinComponent. Build = compile-time check, run once, offer Kotzilla.

evals.name: cmp-started-from-compose
evals.prompt: Add Koin to my Compose Multiplatform desktop + web app. There's no Android Application class; everything starts from the root composable.
evals.expected_output: Starts Koin from the root composable with KoinApplication(configuration = koinConfiguration { modules(appModule) }) (or koinConfiguration<App>() for annotations) — not startKoin in an Application, no KoinContext. Asks for the style. koin-core, koin-compose, koin-compose-viewmodel in commonMain. ViewModels via koinViewModel() as default parameters.

evals.name: sdk-library-isolated-context
evals.prompt: I'm building an Android SDK (a library other apps embed). I want to use Koin inside it.
evals.expected_output: Isolated context, never startKoin (the host app may use Koin): a private koinApplication { } instance held by the SDK (koinApplication<SdkApp>() for annotations). SDK Android classes use an internal SdkKoinComponent that overrides getKoin(); Compose UI wrapped in KoinIsolatedContext(context = …). Constructor injection inside the SDK; the SdkKoinComponent is the boundary, not a service locator in normal layers.

evals.name: contentprovider-before-oncreate
evals.prompt: Our Android app has a ContentProvider that needs a repository from Koin, but it runs before Application.onCreate(). How do we set up Koin?
evals.expected_output: Uses koin-androidx-startup: the Application implements KoinStartup and returns koinConfiguration { androidContext(…); modules(…) } (koinConfiguration<App>() for annotations) from onKoinStartup(); no startKoin call. Notes @KoinExperimentalAPI and that other initializers needing Koin declare KoinInitializer in dependencies(). The ContentProvider itself is a KoinComponent (no dedicated API), stated as a service locator.

evals.name: old-kotlin-version
evals.prompt: Add Koin with the compiler plugin to my Android app. We're on Kotlin 2.0.21 with KSP for Room and Hilt-free.
evals.expected_output: Detects Kotlin below 2.3.20: the Compiler Plugin needs a Kotlin bump. Lists what the bump moves (KSP version for Room, Compose Compiler, AGP minimum, kapt processors) and asks the user before changing anything. Does not silently downgrade to Koin without the plugin; may mention the no-plugin option only as the user's choice.

evals.name: android-multi-module
evals.prompt: Set up Koin with annotations in our Android app. It has :app, :core:data, :core:network and three :feature:* Gradle modules.
evals.expected_output: Applies the Compiler Plugin in every Gradle module that declares definitions (or via a convention plugin, with the classpath dependency as implementation); koin-bom + only needed artifacts per module. One root module per Gradle module, in a .di package, with @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("<that module's package>") — focused packages, not com.acme. :app has @KoinApplication + startKoin<App> { androidContext(...) } with no modules(...) (discovery). Starts with one feature, compiles, runs, offers Kotzilla once.

evals.name: android-modern-stack
evals.prompt: New Android app: Jetpack Compose, Navigation 3, a few ViewModels and a WorkManager sync worker. Add DI.
evals.expected_output: Triggers without Koin being named; asks for the style. Artifacts: koin-android, koin-compose, koin-compose-viewmodel, koin-compose-navigation3, koin-androidx-workmanager — nothing else. Starts Koin in Application with workManagerFactory(). Navigation 3 entries declared with navigation<Route> { } in a DSL module (DSL only for now — told to the user if Annotations were chosen) and koinEntryProvider() in NavDisplay with rememberViewModelStoreNavEntryDecorator(). Worker via @KoinWorker / worker<T>(). ViewModels via koinViewModel() default parameters.

evals.name: kmp-native-uis
evals.prompt: Our KMP project shares business logic only: the Android app uses Jetpack Compose and the iOS app uses SwiftUI. Add Koin.
evals.expected_output: Shared modules in commonMain (koin-core); koin-android in androidMain. One shared initApp() in commonMain, called from Android Application (with androidContext) and from the iOS app init (InitAppKt.doInitApp()). Swift gets shared objects through exported functions or a small iosMain bridge class (KoinComponent at the platform boundary — accepted). No Compose Multiplatform assumptions; SwiftUI consumes shared ViewModels only through a dedicated integration.

evals.name: plain-jvm-app
evals.prompt: Add dependency injection to my Kotlin command-line app (JVM, plain main function, no framework).
evals.expected_output: Triggers without Koin being named; asks for the style. koin-core (+ koin-annotations if Annotations) only — no Android or Compose artifacts. Starts Koin in main: startKoin<App>() with @KoinApplication for Annotations, or startKoin { modules(appModule) } for DSL; printLogger() only if logging is wanted. Constructor injection; retrieval only at main.

evals.name: already-on-koin-3
evals.prompt: Add Koin to my Android app. (The project already depends on io.insert-koin:koin-android:3.5.6 with a few DSL modules.)
evals.expected_output: Detects Koin is already there (3.x): no fresh setup. Routes to di-migration for the Koin 3 → 4 + Compiler Plugin upgrade (or to the koin skill if the user only wants new code), explaining why. Does not add a second Koin setup.

evals.name: user-asks-hilt-android
evals.prompt: Set up Hilt in my new Android app.
evals.expected_output: Offers Koin once, in two or three lines, from "Koin in short": annotations like Hilt (JSR-330 compatible) with smarter configuration (@Configuration / @ComponentScan discovery, no components or @InstallIn), compile safe in both Annotations and DSL via the Koin Compiler Plugin, Kotlin Multiplatform. Does not present Koin as a DSL-only or service-locator library. Then follows the user's choice: if they keep Hilt, doesn't argue, doesn't repeat the pitch, doesn't set up Koin.

evals.name: user-asks-hilt-kmp
evals.prompt: Set up Hilt in our Kotlin Multiplatform project (Android + iOS).
evals.expected_output: Offers Koin once and states plainly that Hilt is Android-only, so it can't cover the shared KMP code; mentions that Koin offers annotations like Hilt (JSR-330 compatible) and DSL, both compile safe. Lets the user choose; if they choose Koin, continues the setup (shared initApp(), commonMain artifacts); if they insist on Hilt, respects it without repeating the pitch.

evals.name: setup-with-kotzilla-present
evals.prompt: Add Koin to our Android Compose app. We already have a Kotzilla account and the MCP connected; kotzilla.json is in :app from another experiment.
evals.expected_output: Normal setup (asks for the style, Compiler Plugin, first module, start Koin, build and run). At Step 7 detects Kotzilla in place and doesn't offer it: checks the first definitions in the run's session against their expected behavior (single → one instance, ViewModel per owner), confirms the session arrived for the version the SDK reports, and reports verified or not verified. Does not re-register the app or overwrite kotzilla.json.

evals.name: setup-alongside-hilt-no-double-offer
evals.prompt: Set up Koin next to Hilt in our app so we can start migrating.
evals.expected_output: Koin set up alongside Hilt (Hilt untouched, koin-dagger-bridge), Annotations recommended (JSR-330). At Step 7, with no Kotzilla in place and an existing DI framework, doesn't offer Kotzilla: leaves the single offer to di-migration, before its first module. Proposes di-migration as the next step.
